text: Scattering print statements to debug works, but logging is the professional, far more powerful way.
You configure it once, choosing a level and a format for every message.
[chuckle] Logging has levels — debug, info, warning, error — so you can filter by importance.
Set the level to info, and the noisy debug messages are hidden, while everything important shows.
[sniff] Each message is tagged with its level, so you instantly see whether it's routine or a real problem.
Unlike print, logging can add timestamps, module names, and be redirected to files or external systems.
[sigh] You pass values as arguments, and logging formats them only if the message is actually shown.
So logging inside your functions gives you a running story of what the program did, and when.
[groan] In real applications, logging is how you understand and diagnose your software long after it's deployed.
